department: Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences — Ph.D. in Integrated Biomedical Sciences (including Neuroscience discipline)

deadline.value: Application opens September 1 with a December 1 submission deadline.

gre_general.value: GRE scores are not required for the Ph.D. in Integrated Biomedical Sciences.
gre_general.quote: GRE scores are not required for applicants applying to the IBMS Graduate Program

gre_subject.value: No ETS GRE Subject Test exists for biomedical sciences or neuroscience, and GRE scores are not required.
gre_subject.quote: GRE scores are not required for applicants applying to the IBMS Graduate Program

also.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: No prior faculty contact or supervisor is needed during the application process; students select a primary discipline during their first year.
supervisor.quote: Do I need to contact faculty prior to applying to a graduate program? No, there is no need to reach out to faculty during the application process.

also.quote: Students admitted into the IBMS identify a “primary discipline of interest” during their first year.

funding.value: Students receive a $35,000 annual stipend, with tuition, fees, and student health insurance covered by the program.
funding.quote: Students receive an annual stipend of $35,000

also.quote: Tuition/Fees and Student Health Insurance are covered by the program

entry_route.value: Applicants must have, or be in the process of completing, a bachelor's degree with a final GPA of 3.0 or above.
entry_route.quote: Applicants to the Integrated Biomedical Sciences (IBMS) Graduate Program must have, or be in the process of completing, a bachelor's degree with a final Grade Point Average of 3.0 or above.

notes: Integrated Biomedical Sciences Ph.D. spans seven disciplines: Biochemical Mechanisms in Medicine, Biology of Aging, Cancer Biology, Cell Biology Genetics & Molecular Medicine, Molecular Immunology & Microbiology, Neuroscience, and Physiology & Pharmacology.
